moat_against: No customer switching costs — diners switch freely in a fragmented, intensely competitive China restaurant market
Delivery-platform dependence and rising delivery mix pressure restaurant margins (delivery ~54% of company sales in Q2 2026)
China consumer softness pins same-store sales near flat (Q2 2026 SSS +1%) and average ticket is falling
KFC brand is licensed from Yum! Brands (royalty drag); Pizza Hut brand ownership only being acquired in 2026
ROIC fell to 8.2% in FY2022 — returns are cyclical, not through-cycle wide-moat level
moat_for: Largest restaurant operator in China — 19,297 stores at Q2 2026 (KFC + Pizza Hut), unmatched store density and brand reach
Proprietary supply chain and procurement scale built over ~40 years, plus food-safety trust that is hard to buy
Digital membership scale — over 270 million active KFC/Pizza Hut members; delivery sales +26% YoY in Q2 2026
ROIC proxy recovered to 19.2% in FY2025 (14.9% / 16.6% / 19.2% over FY2023-25) on stable ~10-11% operating margins
New-store paybacks of 2-3 years and side-by-side modules (KCOFFEE, KPRO, Pizza Hut WOW/Burger Bar) extend the network into lower-tier cities
moat_justification: Scale, brands, supply chain and digital membership give a real but narrow-to-moderate moat: ROIC recovered to 19.2% in FY2025 after an 8.2% FY2022 trough, operating margins hold ~10-11%, but there are no switching costs, competition is intense and fragmented, and the KFC brand is licensed — 6/10, not wide.
name: Yum China Holdings, Inc.
one_liner: Quality China QSR leader, moat 6/10 — does not clear 15% at $45.12 (weighted IRR 12.2%, weighted IV@15% $34.09); it clears 15% only at or below ~$34.
